title: ICAB P6 - Corporate Laws & Practices
summary: Advanced corporate legal practice under Companies Act 1994, BSEC Securities & Exchange rules, Bank Companies Act 1991, Financial Institutions Act, and FERA foreign investment regulations.

all.name: Full Syllabus Tracker
all.blurb: Official 2025 Syllabus chapter and topic tracker for Corporate Laws & Practices. Track your study progress across all syllabus areas.

stages.title: Area 1: Companies Act 1994 Advanced Corporate Practice
stages.name: Area 1: Companies Act 1994 Advanced Corporate Practice
stages.description: Share capital alteration, debentures, mortgages, investigations, amalgamation, and winding up.

nodes.name: Capital Restructuring, Mortgages & Corporate Winding Up
nodes.description: Share capital reduction and variation of shareholder rights; registration of charges, mortgages, and debentures (Section 159); corporate investigations by government; schemes of arrangement and compromise (Sections 228-229); modes of winding up: By High Court, voluntary winding up (members' vs creditors'), and role of official liquidator.
topics: Alteration of share capital: Consolidation, subdivision, cancellation under Section 53
Reduction of share capital: Special resolution and High Court confirmation requirements
Registration of charges and mortgages with RJSC: 21-day timeline, certificate, consequences of non-registration
Investigation into company affairs by Registrar or Government under Section 195
Corporate reconstruction, compromise, and amalgamation procedures under Sections 228 & 229
Modes of winding up: Compulsory winding up by court (grounds under Section 241)
Voluntary winding up: Members' voluntary winding up vs Creditors' voluntary winding up
Powers, duties, and liabilities of Official Liquidators
learningOutcomes: Advise on legal procedure for capital reduction and charge registration.
Draft schemes of compromise and amalgamation under Section 228.
Determine grounds and statutory procedures for winding up a company.
checklists: Read Capital Restructuring, Mortgages & Corporate Winding Up in ICAB Study Manual
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 2: BSEC Securities & Exchange Regulations
stages.name: Area 2: BSEC Securities & Exchange Regulations
stages.description: Securities Rules 2020, Public Issue Rules 2015, Rights Issue Rules, and Listing Regulations.

nodes.name: BSEC Public Issue, Rights Issue & Listing Regulations
nodes.description: Securities and Exchange Ordinance 1969; Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (Public Issue) Rules 2015 (Fixed price method vs Book building method); BSEC (Rights Issue) Rules 2006; Listing Regulations 2015 of DSE/CSE; Corporate Governance Code compliance.
topics: BSEC regulatory framework and market surveillance powers
Public Issue Rules 2015: Eligibility for IPO, minimum paid-up capital, sponsor share lock-in
IPO methods: Fixed Price Method vs Book Building Method (bidding by institutional investors)
Rights Issue Rules: Conditions, eligibility, approval process, and renounceable letters of rights
Private placement of debt securities: BSEC guidelines for sukuk, green bonds, asset-backed securities
Stock Exchange Listing Regulations 2015: Continuous disclosures, price-sensitive information (PSI)
Corporate Governance Code 2018: Mandatory compliance, board composition, and governance audits
learningOutcomes: Formulate IPO proposals under Fixed Price and Book Building methods.
Ensure compliance with BSEC Rights Issue Rules.
Identify Price Sensitive Information (PSI) and fulfill disclosure obligations.
checklists: Read BSEC Public Issue, Rights Issue & Listing Regulations in ICAB Study Manual
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 3: Bank Companies Act & Financial Institutions Act
stages.name: Area 3: Bank Companies Act & Financial Institutions Act
stages.description: Bank Companies Act 1991, licensing, board governance, non-performing loans, and NBFIs.

nodes.name: Banking Regulation, Governance & Non-Performing Loans
nodes.description: Bank Companies Act 1991 (with recent amendments): Licensing by Bangladesh Bank, capital requirements (BASEL III overview), board constitution, single borrower exposure limits, classification of non-performing loans (NPLs); Financial Institutions Act 1993 for Non-Bank Financial Institutions (NBFIs).
topics: Licensing and business restrictions of banking companies under Bank Companies Act 1991
Board of directors rules: Maximum directors from one family, independent directors, tenure limits
Single borrower exposure limit and related party lending restrictions
Non-Performing Loans (NPL): Classification categories (Sub-standard, Doubtful, Bad/Loss) and provisioning
Powers of Bangladesh Bank: Prompt Corrective Action (PCA), appointing observer/administrator
Financial Institutions Act 1993: Regulation of NBFIs, leasing, and merchant banks
learningOutcomes: Apply Bank Companies Act restrictions on lending and family directorships.
Classify loans and calculate mandatory loan-loss provisions.
Explain Bangladesh Bank supervisory interventions under PCA.
checklists: Read Banking Regulation, Governance & Non-Performing Loans in ICAB Study Manual
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 4: Foreign Exchange Regulation Act & BIDA
stages.name: Area 4: Foreign Exchange Regulation Act & BIDA
stages.description: FERA 1947, foreign investment approvals, profit repatriation, and external commercial borrowing.

nodes.name: Foreign Exchange (FERA), BIDA & Profit Repatriation
nodes.description: Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 (FERA): Authorized dealers, current account vs capital account transactions; Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA) registration; opening branch/liaison offices; repatriation of dividends, royalties, and franchise fees; External Commercial Borrowings (ECB).
topics: FERA 1947 framework: Foreign currency dealing, authorized dealers, central bank circulars
Current account convertibility vs Capital account restrictions in Bangladesh
BIDA registration procedures for foreign direct investment (FDI)
Establishing Branch Office, Liaison/Representative Office, and permission renewals
Legal guidelines for outward remittance of dividend, technical fees, royalty, and consultancy fees
Foreign borrowing: External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) approvals by Bangladesh Bank committee
Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012 and compliance by reporting agencies
learningOutcomes: Guide foreign investors through BIDA registration and office setup.
Fulfill regulatory compliance for profit and dividend repatriation under FERA.
Navigate Bangladesh Bank approvals for foreign currency commercial loans.
checklists: Read Foreign Exchange (FERA), BIDA & Profit Repatriation in ICAB Study Manual
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)
